name: Revenue Recognition
description: Case-pool variant of Revenue Calculation, for Problem Recognition.
business_contexts: a boutique furniture maker closing out its first full year of online sales
a mobile game studio wrapping up a seasonal in-app promotion
a regional ticketing platform reviewing a completed concert series
a subscription meal-kit company closing its books for the quarter
a wholesale distributor totaling a completed shipping cycle
question_patterns: How much did the client bring in from this product line before any costs are considered?
What did the client's top line come out to for the period?
Before subtracting anything, what was the total amount the client collected from customers?
What figure lands on the very first line of the client's income statement for this period?
key_insight: Revenue is the top line before any cost is subtracted — price times quantity, nothing else.
common_mistakes: Subtracting costs before arriving at revenue, which conflates revenue with profit
Multiplying price by a different volume figure than the one actually sold
framework_soundbite: Revenue is price times quantity — the starting line, not the finish line.
